pages.title: Three ways to take it
text: - **Tincture**: drink it. The remedy lasts **3 minutes** and you get the bottle back.

- **Salve**: use it to lay it on yourself, or **use it on someone else**: a friend, a villager, your familiar. It heals **3 hearts** at once, lifts **every** harmful effect, and carries the remedy for half as long as a tincture.
- **Incense**: seat it in a [Ritual Brazier](ritual_brazier) and it burns for everyone around. See below.
**Every remedy lifts [Spirit Sickness](spirit_sickness).**

pages.title: What each family brews
text: - **Kindling** (Ember): Strength.
- **Quickening** (Bolt): Speed.
- **Cooling** (Chill): Fire Resistance.
- **Antidote** (Venom): lifts poison, wither, hunger and nausea.
- **Featherfall** (Gust): Slow Falling.
- **Rootedness** (Root): Resistance.

pages.title: What each family brews, continued
text: - **Bulwark** (Shove): Absorption.
- **Clear Sight** (Weave): Night Vision, lifts blindness.
- **Restoring** (Weaken): Haste, lifts weakness and slowness.
- **Vigour** (Hound): Health Boost.
- **Mending** (Quiet): Regeneration.
The colour of the brew is the colour of its reagent, so you can tell them apart in your pack.

pages.title: The totem's voice
text: The totem nearest the kettle while it brewed adds its own gift, shown on the tooltip:
- **Earth**: grants 2 hearts of absorption.  - **Fire**: lasts half again as long.
- **Water**: one level stronger.  - **Air**: heals 2 hearts at once.
- **Spirit**: adds 10 seconds of Regeneration.  - **Loom**: lasts twice as long, but stays at level I.

pages.title: Burning incense
text: Use incense on a Ritual Brazier to seat it; it holds up to **16** sticks of one brew. It burns on its own, with **no seal and no Pulse**.

Every two seconds everyone within **8 blocks**, players and bonded familiars, gets the remedy for 12 seconds, and familiars are mended a heart. Each stick lasts **30 seconds**. A redstone signal on the brazier puts it out; sneak-use it with an empty hand, with no seal seated, to take the incense back.
It is the best way to keep a whole camp on its feet through a long night.
